facts.statement: Hoplosuchus is known from a single skeleton found in the Morrison Formation of Utah during road construction.
facts.quote: It is so far only known definitely from one specimen, a skeleton collected from sandstone of the Upper Jurassic-age Morrison Formation rocks at Dinosaur National Monument, Utah, during road construction.

facts.statement: The known specimen of Hoplosuchus was approximately 20 cm long, though it might have been a juvenile.
facts.quote: The individual was small, approximately 20 cm long, although it may have been very young.

facts.statement: Hoplosuchus had relatively long limbs, indicating it was a terrestrial animal.
facts.quote: The limbs were relatively long, suggesting that the animal was terrestrial.

facts.statement: Due to its small size, Hoplosuchus likely ate insects and small vertebrates, possibly being carnivorous or omnivorous.
facts.quote: Given its small size, it probably ate insects and small vertebrates; it may have been carnivorous or omnivorous.

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore named the genus Hoplosuchus in 1926, with H. kayi as the type species.
facts.quote: Charles W. Gilmore named Hoplosuchus in 1926; the type species is H. kayi.

facts.statement: A 2017 cladistic analysis recovered Hoplosuchus as a member of the family Protosuchidae.
facts.quote: A 2017 cladistic analysis of Cassissuchus recovered it as a member of Protosuchidae.

facts.statement: Hoplosuchus lived during the Tithonian stage, between 149.2 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 145.06 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Two rows of wide, rectangular bony scutes ran along the back of Hoplosuchus.
